page.title: Marbella Yacht Charter for Ironman 2049 Recovery Day

data.meta_description: Book an Ironman Marbella 2049 recovery yacht charter from Puerto Banús. Relax on the Azimut 39 from €749/2h with skipper, drinks & snacks included.

faq.q: How soon after the Ironman Marbella 2049 can I board a recovery charter?
faq.a: Most athletes board within 1–2 hours of finishing. Our boats depart from Puerto Banús, which is a short walk or taxi from the finish area. We recommend booking a 2-hour charter starting at your estimated finish time – you can adjust on the day via WhatsApp.

faq.q: Which boat is best for a small recovery group?
faq.a: For 5–8 people, the Astondoa 40 (9 pax) or Azimut 39 (11 pax) are ideal. Both are Tier A boats at €749/2h or €2,299/8h. They have shaded seating, a small cabin for changing, and a swim platform for a gentle dip.

faq.q: Can we bring our own recovery food or supplements?
faq.a: Yes, you can bring your own food and drinks. However, our charters already include water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. If you need specific recovery shakes or electrolyte drinks, just bring them – there’s a cooler on board.

faq.q: Are there any extra costs on top of the charter price?
faq.a: No. The price includes the licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, safety equipment, Spanish IVA (21%), and all listed drinks and snacks. The only optional extra is a jet ski on the Mangusta 80 – but that’s included free for the first 4-hour charter.

faq.q: What if the sea is rough after the race?
faq.a: The skipper monitors conditions and will suggest a sheltered route, such as staying close to the coast around Cabopino or heading into the calm waters of the Marbella Marina area. If conditions are unsafe, we’ll reschedule or refund – safety comes first.

faq.q: Can we book a charter for the day after the race?
faq.a: Absolutely. Many athletes book a recovery charter for the following day to enjoy the coast without the race-day rush. The Azimut 58 Flybridge and Mangusta 80 are popular for this – both depart from Puerto Banús and can accommodate up to 12 guests.

faq.q: Do you provide any special recovery amenities like ice baths or massage?
faq.a: We don’t have onboard ice baths or massage therapists, but we do provide a shaded deck, comfortable seating, and a swim platform. You can bring your own compression gear or float – the calm water off Cala del Faro is perfect for gentle floating.

data.body_html:
Crossing the finish line of Ironman Marbella 2049 is a monumental achievement. After months of training, your body deserves more than a quick shower and a crowded restaurant. A private yacht charter from Puerto Banús offers the ultimate recovery: gentle sea breeze, cold drinks, and a soft place to sit while your legs finally rest. Whether you want a quiet 2-hour cruise or a full day of floating, our fleet is ready to turn your post-race hours into a mini-holiday.

Why a Yacht Is the Best Recovery After Ironman

Post-race recovery isn’t just about lying down – it’s about reducing muscle soreness and mental fatigue. The gentle rocking of a boat, the cool marine air, and the chance to elevate your legs on a sun lounger all help. Plus, you avoid the crowded pools and busy beaches. A 2-hour charter from Puerto Banús gives you enough time to decompress, hydrate, and enjoy the coastline without any physical effort.

Our Recovery-Ready Fleet

We have boats for every group size. For solo athletes or pairs, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) is a compact option. For small groups of up to 11, the Azimut 39 and Astondoa 40 are perfect – both are Tier A boats at €749/2h or €2,299/8h. If you’ve finished with a group of friends or family, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is a luxurious choice, with a minimum 4-hour charter at €4,719 that includes a free jet ski – if you have energy left to try it.

What’s Included in Every Charter

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). You’ll also get unlimited water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks. That means no hidden costs – just show up with your towel and recovery gear. For longer charters, we can arrange a more substantial meal on request (at extra cost).

Recovery-Focused Itineraries from Puerto Banús

Our skippers know the calmest spots. A popular recovery route is heading east towards Cabopino – a quiet marina with sandy coves. Or cruise west to Cala del Faro, a sheltered cove where you can anchor and float in the clear water. If you prefer to stay close, a slow loop around the Marbella Marina and past the Golden Mile offers a gentle sightseeing tour without any chop.

Pricing and Booking for Ironman Week

We know Ironman Marbella week is busy, so book early. For the Azimut 39 and Astondoa 40, prices are fixed: €749 for 2 hours, €2,299 for 8 hours. The Mangusta 80 starts at €4,719 for 4 hours (jet ski included). All other boats – including the Azimut 58 Flybridge and Ferretti 94 – are priced on request via WhatsApp. We’ll confirm availability within minutes.

What to Expect on Board

Your skipper will welcome you at the boat, help you aboard, and brief you on the safety equipment. Once you’re settled, you can choose your music, ask for a slower speed, or just nap on the sun pads. The crew is used to athletes – they’ll have towels and extra water ready. You’re not expected to do anything but relax.

Combine with a Post-Race Celebration

If you’re celebrating with teammates or family, why not turn your recovery charter into a party? The Mangusta 80 has a spacious flybridge and a jet ski for adrenaline seekers. For a more refined gathering, the Canados 86 (26m, 12 pax) offers elegant salons. All charters depart from Puerto Banús, so you can step off straight into the marina’s restaurants and bars.
